Total distributable earnings were $1.72 billion, or $0.73 a share, up 16% per share from $0.63; before realizations they were $1.50 billion, or $0.64 a share, up 14% [1].

Asset management raised $25 billion in the quarter and $123 billion year to date; fee-bearing capital rose 13% to $682 billion and fee-related earnings rose 15% [1].

After the quarter, the infrastructure flagship fund drew $13 billion of new commitments, taking it to $26 billion; Brookfield says it will be the largest infrastructure fund ever raised once the first close is finalized [1].

Brookfield Corporation said third-quarter distributable earnings, its main measure of cash earnings, rose 16% per share to $1.72 billion, or $0.73 a share, from $1.49 billion, or $0.63, a year earlier [1]. Distributable earnings before realizations, which strip out carried interest, rose 14% per share to $0.64 and reached a record $5.8 billion, or $2.47 a share, over the last twelve months [1]. Net income of the consolidated business was $1.91 billion, up from $284 million, with $1.31 billion attributable to Brookfield shareholders [1].

"Our asset management business raised $25 billion, wealth solutions delivered 22% earnings growth, and our operating businesses continued to generate resilient cash flows," President Nick Goodman said [1].

Where the earnings came from

Asset management contributed $755 million of distributable earnings, up from $687 million, as fee-bearing capital grew 13% to $682 billion [1]. Fundraising reached $123 billion through the third quarter, including records of $1.2 billion for the infrastructure private wealth strategy and $1.5 billion for the super-core infrastructure strategy [1]. Since quarter-end the infrastructure flagship fund has taken $13 billion of additional commitments, for $26 billion to date [1].

Wealth solutions earned $511 million, up from $420 million, helped by the Just Group acquisition in the second quarter that took insurance assets to nearly $200 billion [1]. Operating businesses contributed $467 million, up from $366 million, and Brookfield realized $222 million of net carried interest [1]. Accumulated unrealized carried interest grew to $13.0 billion [1].

Brookfield repurchased more than $300 million of Class A shares since its last report, for $889 million so far this year, and said in its shareholder letter that it bought as "our share price traded off like most non-big technology securities" [1][2]. It ended the quarter with $207 billion of deployable capital and declared a dividend of $0.07 a share payable Dec. 31 [1].

The letter points to Westinghouse, which Brookfield controls, as a growth engine: a framework with the US and Korean governments under which Korea will invest up to $120 billion in reactors built on US federal land, and 14 reactors in construction with another 40 coming [2]. It also says AI is driving "unprecedented investment in data centers, compute, and related infrastructure," where Brookfield supplies power, data centers and compute under long-term contracts [2]. Its AI infrastructure venture with Qatar recently made its first deal at the Drax power station in the UK.

Brookfield expects to complete its corporate simplification on Dec. 1, with shares of the new Brookfield Corporation Ltd. due to start trading under the BN symbol on the NYSE and TSX on Dec. 3 [1].
